|lore=“I’m not afraid.” “Oh. You will be. You will be.” One of the lessons Luke learned was that fear of the unknown can be stronger than fear of the known.
|game_text=''When drawn for destiny, may place a non-[Immune to Alter] Effect on table in owner’s Used Pile.'' OR Lose the top card of your Reserve Deck to make a just drawn destiny lost.
|printings={{Card versions/Fear (Dagobah)}}
|notes=The remastered slip for Fear uses the official text dated 4 December 2006. The published Set 5 editions are linked as [[Fear (V) (Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time)|Original]] and [[Fear (V) (Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time) (Errata)|Remastered (2006)]]. The first sheet was released 30 May 2003 and became tournament legal on 6 June. The remastered wording specifies that the Effect being moved to its owner’s Used Pile is on table. The original refers to an Effect in the same drawn-destiny action, subject to the [https://web.archive.org/web/20090816063441id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/AR/AR1.7.1.pdf#page=22 period rule on active cards]. The [https://web.archive.org/web/20090816063441id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/AR/AR1.7.1.pdf#page=29 period example] distinguishes drawing Fear for destiny from using its value while it is stacked. This is the Set 5 Interrupt based on [[Fear]].
|sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20071024154714/http://www.swccgpc.com/Resources/VirtualCards5.pdf#page=4 VirtualCards5.pdf] (Players Committee Remaster sheet, Internet Archive 24 October 2007) — official text as of 4 December 2006 (errata to card #49 on 14 September 2007); page 4, slip 36. Slip image and game text from this sheet.
